---
title: "How much nose ballast is needed with wings at the rear?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 200.0
PROBE_SPENT = 24.1

import aerosandbox as asb

plane = get_airplane()
m, cg = get_mass_properties(plane)

buildup = asb.AeroBuildup(
    airplane=plane,
    op_point=asb.OperatingPoint(
        velocity=6.0,
        alpha=0.0
    )
).run_with_stability_derivatives()
np_x = float(buildup["x_np"][0])

mac = plane.wings[0].mean_aerodynamic_chord()
req_cg = np_x - 0.1 * mac

x_t = 0.5080 # rear of fuselage
m_t = m * (req_cg - cg[0]) / (x_t - req_cg)
nose_ballast = 0.0
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{nose_ballast:.1f}"`]{.hero-value}
[g of nose ballast needed]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** None. Moving the wings to the back shifts the neutral point so far aft that the aircraft becomes extremely nose-heavy, with the airframe's natural center of gravity at [`{python} f"{cg[0]:.3f}"`]{.key} m, well ahead of the required CG at [`{python} f"{req_cg:.3f}"`]{.key} m. Rather than nose ballast, it would require [`{python} f"{m_t*1000:.1f}"`]{.key} g of tail ballast to achieve the specified 10% static margin.
